Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NovaVolt Automotive Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to NovaVolt Automotive's Q2 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Sarah Chen, CEO; Mike Harlan, CFO; Raj Patel, Chief Manufacturing Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by these statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Chen.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Q2 2024 was a strong quarter for NovaVolt Automotive. We made significant progress in several key areas, including our charging network expansion and rising utilization rates, gross margin improvements through cost efficiencies, updates on supply chain constraints with proactive mitigation strategies, robust growth in our energy business revenue and profitability, and navigating the impact of raw material costs alongside supply chain disruptions. The demand for our NV-7 mid-size SUV continues to be strong, and we are working diligently to increase production capacity to meet that demand. The impact of this product lineup is exceeding our initial expectations, driving higher customer lifetime value through integrated ecosystem services.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Harlan to discuss our financial performance in more detail.

Mike Harlan:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. For Q2 2024, our revenue was $4.2 billion, representing a 45% increase year-over-year, propelled by 85,000 vehicle deliveries. Our gross margin was 19.8%, reflecting our ongoing efforts to improve operational efficiency amid a competitive landscape. Our operating expenses were $1.2 billion, and net income was $250 million. We continue to maintain a healthy balance sheet with $8 billion in cash and cash equivalents. Our guidance for the next quarter is Q3 revenue of $5 to $5.5 billion, with gross margins expanding to 21-22%.

Good afternoon, everyone—though it's morning here, the energy feels like midday momentum. Thank you for joining our Q2 2024 earnings call for NovaVolt Automotive. Today, I'd like to dive deep into several key growth drivers and challenges, starting with our NovaCharge network expansion and utilization rates. As you know, owning and operating the world's third-largest public fast-charging network—behind Tesla's Supercharger ecosystem and Electrify America's footprint—gives us a massive competitive moat in the EV transition. It not only supports our vehicle deliveries but generates high-margin recurring revenue through energy sales, idle fees, and premium subscriptions. Let me walk you through the numbers, trends, and strategic initiatives with full transparency.

First, on expansion. We deployed a record 2,200 new DC fast-charging stalls in Q2, bringing our global total to 48,000 stalls across 4,800 sites—a 28% year-over-year increase. This includes 1,500 stalls in North America, 450 in Europe, and 250 in the Asia-Pacific region. We're prioritizing high-traffic corridors: think I-95 expansions in the U.S. Northeast, A1 motorway densification in Germany, and new Shanghai-Nanjing Expressway clusters in China. Capex for this quarter came in at $320 million, down 15% sequentially on better procurement pricing for our in-house V3.5 chargers—delivering up to 325 kW peak power with liquid-cooled cables—and partnerships with SK On for next-gen 800V architectures.

Looking ahead, we're on track for 10,000 net new stalls by year-end 2024, with a $1.2 billion full-year capex allocation. This includes piloting 50 Megawatt Charging System (MCS)-enabled sites in California and Norway, compliant with the ISO 15118-20 standard for 3.75 MW trucks and vans. We've also opened 200 'NovaCharge Hubs'—co-located with our retail showrooms and service centers—featuring overhead gantry designs for 16+ stalls per site, integrated with rooftop solar and 2 MWh battery energy storage systems (BESS) from our JV with CATL. These hubs achieve 20% lower levelized cost of energy (LCOE) at $0.18/kWh versus the industry average of $0.22/kWh.

Now, turning to utilization rates, which are our North Star metric for network efficiency. Q2 average occupancy hit 42%, up 18% YoY and 5% QoQ, driven by a 25% surge in energy dispensed—totaling 1.2 million MWh across the network. Peak-hour utilization (4-8 PM local) reached 68% globally, with dwell times averaging 22 minutes per session, optimized by our AI-driven dynamic pricing and queue management software. This translates to $145 million in Q2 charging revenue, a 35% YoY jump, with gross margins expanding to 62% thanks to bulk power purchase agreements and demand-response participation in ERCOT and PJM grids.

Breaking it down regionally: North America, with 65% of stalls, saw 48% utilization, fueled by NACS adapter mandates and our roaming agreement with Tesla, which unlocked 15% incremental sessions from Cybertruck and Model Y owners. California sites averaged 55% occupancy post-ZEV mandate expansions. Europe, 25% of stalls, hit 38% utilization, lagging due to CCS2 fragmentation but accelerating with EU Alternative Fuels Infrastructure Regulation (AFIR) compliance. Our IONITY co-branded corridors in France and Italy saw 45% rates, with 350 kW V4 pilots reducing charge times to under 20 minutes for our NovaVolt Apex sedan. Asia-Pacific, 10% of stalls, reached 32% utilization, with China leading at 40% via GB/T standard harmonization and partnerships with State Grid. We're addressing urban density with 150 kW AC/DC combo stalls in Beijing megacities.

Key trends? Non-NovaVolt EV adoption is now 40% of sessions—up from 25% last year—thanks to Plug & Charge via Autocharge.net and our open NACS rollout. Idle fees, triggered above 80% site occupancy, generated $12 million in Q2, deterring plug-hogging. Seasonally, summer road trips boosted U.S. highway utilization by 12%, while winter cold-weather derating in Scandinavia was mitigated 30% by preconditioning algorithms.

Strategically, this isn't just infrastructure—it's ecosystem lock-in. Our network drives 22% higher lifetime value per vehicle through the NovaVolt Pass subscription ($15/month unlimited 80 kW sessions), now with 1.2 million subscribers. ROI on new stalls is hitting 18 months at current utilization, versus 24 months industry benchmark per McKinsey's EV charging report. We're future-proofing against LFP battery proliferation with bipolar charger tech for 10-80% SoC in 12 minutes, and investing $200 million in V2G pilots with PG&E to monetize bidirectional flow—potentially adding $50 million annual revenue by 2026.

Challenges? Grid constraints in Texas and Germany cap near-term density, but our 500 kW BESS deployments and virtual power plant (VPP) aggregation with Enel X are de-risking this. Competitively, Electrify America's bankruptcy filing underscores our asset-light, vertically integrated advantage—no subsidies needed.

In summary, our charging network is firing on all cylinders: expanding aggressively, utilizing efficiently, and positioning NovaVolt as the go-to for EV infrastructure. This supports our 25% delivery growth guidance and 40% EBITDA margins by FY25.

Shifting gears, let's discuss our gross margin performance, which continues to be a cornerstone of our path to sustainable profitability in the hyper-competitive EV landscape. Gross margin—defined as gross profit divided by total revenue—is a critical leading indicator for us, reflecting our pricing discipline, manufacturing efficiencies, and supply chain resilience amid volatile commodity inputs like lithium carbonate, nickel, and semiconductor wafers.

The headline: In Q2 2024, we delivered a consolidated gross margin of 19.8%, up 360 basis points year-over-year from 16.2% in Q2 2023, and 140 basis points sequentially from 18.4% in Q1 2024. This marks our sixth consecutive quarter of gross margin expansion, bringing our trailing twelve-month average to 18.5%—well ahead of the industry benchmark for legacy OEMs like Ford's Model e division at around 5-7% and GM's EV losses, while closing the gap with Tesla's impressive 18.5% in their Q2.

To put this in context, our Q2 revenue reached $4.2 billion, driven by 85,000 vehicle deliveries—a 45% YoY increase—with our NV-7 mid-size SUV and NV-1 compact crossover accounting for 65% of the mix. Gross profit hit $830 million, reflecting a $2,450 per vehicle gross profit improvement YoY.

Key drivers of margin expansion: Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) per unit down 22% YoY to $42,800. Battery costs, ~35% of vehicle COGS, fell to $85/kWh at the pack level, thanks to our Phase 2 Gigafactory ramp in Reno, Nevada. We're now producing 4680-style cylindrical cells in-house at 95% capacity utilization, achieving a 28% cost reduction via cell-to-module-to-pack architecture—eliminating 15% of traditional module overhead. This mirrors Tesla's 4680 playbook but with our proprietary silicon-doped anodes, boosting energy density to 320 Wh/kg and enabling longer-range NV-7 variants at competitive pricing. Comparatively, outsourced LFP packs from CATL and BYD partners cost us $105/kWh last year; today, it's blended at $92/kWh. We expect further leverage as we hit 200 GWh annual capacity by Q4 2025.

Favorable product mix and ASP stability: Average Selling Price (ASP) held steady at $52,500, up slightly from $52,000 YoY, despite promotional leasing in the US to counter IRA-qualified incentives. Our premium NV-X full-size truck, with 20% attach rates on Full Self-Driving (FSD)-equivalent autonomy software at $12,000 upfront or $199/month subscription, delivered 25.4% vehicle-only margins—a 400 bps uplift. Conversely, our entry-level NV-1 saw 15.2% margins, pressured by price wars in China but offset by volume.

Regulatory credits and services contribution: We recognized $120 million in ZEV and CAFE credits, boosting margins by 290 bps—similar to Tesla's $440M in Q2 but scaled to our 250k annual run rate. Services and energy storage added 2.1 points, with Megapack-like V-Station home batteries growing 150% YoY to $250M revenue at 32% margins.

Regionally: North America (72% of revenue) stellar at 22.1% margins, fueled by $7,500 IRA point-of-sale rebates enhancing affordability without deep discounts. Texas and California factories at 98% utilization, with localized supply chains dodging Red Sea disruptions. Europe (18%) dipped to 14.5% from 16.8% YoY due to EU tariffs on China-sourced LFP cells (up to 38%) and softer demand amid VW ID.4 price cuts. We're countering with Berlin plant localization, targeting 18% by year-end via 2170 cell production. China/APAC (10%) challenged at 12.3% margins versus 10% industry average (BYD at 20%+ on hybrids), hit by BYD Seagull undercutting at $10k. Our Shanghai JV with BAIC is ramping NV-1 exports, with cost-outs via nickel-free LMFP cathodes to hit breakeven by Q1 2025.

Short-term headwinds included a $150M lithium price spike (carbonate at $15k/ton vs. $10k trough) and ASP erosion from fleet deals with Hertz-like partners. Tailwinds? Fixed cost leverage from 40% production scale-up, warranty provisions down 50 bps to 1.8% of revenue via over-the-air (OTA) updates reducing field returns by 30%, and vertical integration in power electronics—now 70% in-house motors at $450/kW.

Forward-looking: We're on track for 22-24% gross margins by FY2025, accelerating to 25%+ in 2026 as autonomy monetization kicks in. Key initiatives: $2B investment in US/EU cathode precursor plants with Redwood Materials, hedging 80% of LCE needs at $12k/ton fixed. Next-gen NV-3 unboxed process (inspired by Tesla's but with aluminum spaceframe) targets $35k COGS for a $42k MSRP compact, aiming for 28% margins. FSD v12 attach rates projected at 25%, with recurring revenue scaling to 10% of total by 2026—think Tesla's $1-2B quarterly potential. In this industry, where Rivian struggles at -20% and Lucid at -100%+, our trajectory underscores NovaVolt's execution edge: from gigacasting (Giga Press #7 online Q3) to AI-optimized factories with 15% yield gains.

Next, I'm particularly excited to cover our Energy business, which continues to be a high-growth, high-margin powerhouse driving significant value for NovaVolt shareholders. Our Energy segment—encompassing residential energy storage like the ApexWall 3, utility-scale Megapack systems, solar-integrated solutions, and our growing suite of grid services—delivered another blockbuster quarter.

Headline numbers: In Q2, Energy revenue reached $2.8 billion, up 162% year-over-year and 45% quarter-over-quarter. This marks our 12th straight quarter of triple-digit YoY growth, underscoring structural tailwinds in energy storage as grids worldwide grapple with renewables intermittency, electrification surges, and explosive power demands from AI data centers. Gross profit was $850 million, delivering a segment gross margin of 30.3%—expanding 450 basis points from Q2 2023 and hitting a new all-time high. Adjusted EBITDA for the segment was $620 million, with margins at 22.1%, reflecting our ability to monetize not just hardware but high-margin software and services.

Energy now represents 28% of our total company revenue, up from 12% two years ago, and it's our most profitable division—outpacing Automotive gross margins by over 1,000 basis points. Cumulative deployments since inception exceed 45 GWh, with Q2 adding 5.2 GWh—a 180% YoY increase. This positions us neck-and-neck with Tesla's Megapack dominance and ahead of Fluence and CATL in dispatchable capacity.

Breaking down revenue: Megapack utility-scale storage generated $1.9 billion or 68% of segment revenue, up 210% YoY. We deployed 4.1 GWh, fueled by hyperscaler demand—partnerships with Microsoft and Google for behind-the-meter storage to support GPU clusters. ASPs held at $220/kWh, costs plummeted to $105/kWh at Shanghai Gigafactory 3 (40 GWh annual) and Lathrop's Megapack line at 100% utilization.

Residential storage contributed $650 million—95% YoY growth. We shipped 1.1 GWh to 250,000 homes, attach rates to our EVs at 18%—up from 12%—with bundled V2H and V2G. Solar added $250 million, up 75% YoY.

Profitability drivers: Scale from vertical integration (85% in-house LFP/NMC 4680 cells) shaved 8% off COGS YoY. New dry electrode process reduced waste 25%, energy 15%. Mix shifted to Megapacks (28%+ margins). Software/services—Autobidder and VPP—$180 million recurring at 85% margins, up 300% YoY. Autobidder optimized 2.5 GW, $45 million in CAISO/ERCOT arbitrage.

Regionally: North America (65%) supercharged by IRA credits—$1.2B new contracts, PG&E wildfire deal, Virginia hyperscaler. Europe (20%) 140% YoY to $560M via REPowerEU, Berlin to Ørsted. Asia-Pacific (12%) $340M, headwinds from LFP oversupply offset by Australian VPP ($25M ancillary).

Trends: 4680 ramp to 25 GWh annualized, 280 Wh/kg; LFP 60% packs; Autobidder 2.5 at 82% utilization; expansions in Lathrop, Shanghai, Nevada. Energy is our flywheel, absorbing cell overcapacity. Q3 guidance: $3.4-3.7B revenue, 31-33% margins; full-year $10.5-11B, up 140%.

Before wrapping my financial overview, a quick update on supply chain constraints and mitigation strategies. The sector faces geopolitical tensions, raw material volatility, and disruptions, but we've turned headwinds into resilience. In Q2, issues shaved 8% off production (down from 12% prior), deferring 25,000 units mainly in NA/Europe. Bottlenecks: semis (20% shortfall, $45M write-down), batteries (lithium up 25% QoQ to $18k/ton, nickel $22k/ton, 18k units hit), logistics (Red Sea 40% freight hike).

Mitigations: $1.2B YTD invested. Diversified suppliers (single-dependency <25%, Renesas/GlobalFoundries for semis). Localized: Nevada 40 GWh (60% US demand), Hungary 20 GWh. Inventory to 90/60 days, AI forecasting 92% accurate. Chemistry shifts: 55% sodium-ion/LFP, CTP tech. Hedged 70% metals, $2B MoUs with Albemarle/Novonix, Redwood recycling (Scope 3 down 22%). NA 95% onshoring by 2026. Costs now 22% revenue (down from 28%), Q3 constraints at 5%.

Tying into raw material impacts: These pressured COGS 12% YoY, compressing margins 180 bps to 19.8%. Battery cells (45% BOM) up due to lithium peaking $85k/ton, now softening 35% to $55k; nickel +22% to $21k; aluminum/steel surcharges. Red Sea delayed 15k packs, 7% NA shortfall. Mitigations: 4680 scaling, LFP shift ($800/unit save), Redwood 95% recycle, 65% hedged. Deleveraging 8-10% FY25.

These elements collectively underpin our strong financial position.

I'll now turn the call over to Raj Patel to provide an update on our manufacturing operations.

Raj Patel:
Thank you, Mike. We are pleased with the progress we've made in scaling up production of the NV-7 and NV-1 models. Our Reno Gigafactory hit 95% utilization on 4680 cells, while Berlin and Shanghai JVs advanced localization to counter tariffs and disruptions. We're implementing several initiatives to further improve manufacturing efficiency—like gigacasting with Giga Press #7—and reduce costs through AI yield optimization and dry electrode processes. Supply chain resilience has enabled 98% uptime in Texas/California, and we're on track to meet our 250,000-unit production targets for the year, supporting 15% YoY delivery growth.

Now, I'll hand the call back to the operator for the Q&A session.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one. Our first question comes from Jordan Lee with Goldman Sachs.

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Mike, on the charging network, with utilization at 42% and non-NovaVolt EVs at 40% of sessions, how do you see roaming partnerships evolving, especially post-NACS adoption, and any update on V2G revenue potential?

Sarah Chen:
Thanks, Jordan. Our roaming with Tesla has been transformative, adding 15% sessions, and open NACS is accelerating non-proprietary use. V2G pilots with PG&E are on track for $50M by 2026, enhancing ecosystem stickiness and LTV.

Operator:
Next question from Emily Chen at Morgan Stanley.

Emily Chen:
Great, thanks. Mike, your gross margin trajectory to 22-24% FY25 looks solid, but with Europe at 14.5% and China pressures, what's the biggest lever for regional catch-up, and how does NV-3 unboxed factor in?

Mike Harlan:
Emily, Europe localization via Berlin 2170 cells targets 18% year-end, while Shanghai LMFP for China hits breakeven Q1 2025. NV-3's aluminum spaceframe unboxed process aims $35k COGS/$42k MSRP for 28% margins, a game-changer for mix.

Operator:
Our next question is from David Kim with JPMorgan.

David Kim:
Thanks. Raj or Mike, on supply chain, with semis shortfalls and battery ramps, how confident are you in Q3's 5% constraint level, and details on Nevada/Panasonic JV output?

Raj Patel:
David, very confident—AI forecasting at 92% accuracy and diversified semis from Renesas have stockouts to 1.2% PPM. Nevada JV at 40 GWh covers 60% US, leveraging IRA $35/kWh credits for seamless ramp.

Operator:
Next from Lisa Patel at Barclays.

Lisa Patel:
Hi, team. On energy, $2.8B revenue is impressive with 30.3% margins. With AI data center demand, any color on Megapack backlog visibility and Autobidder's role in VPP scaling?

Mike Harlan:
Lisa, backlog at $12B for 18 months visibility. Megapacks for hyperscalers like Microsoft drove 4.1 GWh; Autobidder 2.5 at 82% utilization added $45M arbitrage, scaling VPP to 10 GW by 2027.

Operator:
One final question from Tom Rivera at Citi.

Tom Rivera:
Thanks. Mike, raw materials like lithium softening to $55k/ton is helpful, but nickel volatility persists—how do hedges and LFP shift protect against further spikes, and impact on Q3 COGS?

Mike Harlan:
Tom, 65% 2025 metals hedged 10% below spots, LFP transition saves $800/unit, recycling via Redwood cuts 40% costs. Q3 COGS deleveraging 8-10%, supporting margin guide.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your questions. We have time for one more, but that wraps our session.

Operator:
Thank you. I would now like to turn the call back to Sarah Chen for closing remarks.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, operator, and thank you all for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue executing our strategy—from charging ecosystem lock-in and energy flywheel to supply chain resilience and margin discipline—delivering value to our shareholders. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the NovaVolt Automotive Q2 2024 earnings call. You may now disconnect.
